utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Good morning, Madam Registrar. Could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Good morning, Your Honours. This is the case number IT-99-36-T, the Prosecutor versus Radoslav Brdjanin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Brdjanin, good morning to you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I take it that you are following what I am saying in a language that you can understand.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If at any time that doesn't happen, please let me know. Appearances for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Anna Richterova for the Prosecution, assisted by Denise Gustin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning to you, and thank you. Appearances for Radoslav Brdjanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. I'm John Ackerman. I'm here with David Cunningham and Lidija Lacroix who is substituting today as an interpreter for us. I would ask in advance your permission to leave at some point during the morning, and I don't know whether I'll do that or not, but I'm not feeling particularly well today --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You feel free. Even if you want to leave now, Mr. Ackerman, you have the Court's -- the Tribunal's -- the Chamber's understanding.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Well, I think Mr. Cunningham is prepared for the witnesses today and can probably carry forward without too much difficulty in my absence, so I may depart. I may start feeling better in a few minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Ackerman. By the way, may I ask you if the binders did arrive yesterday? Did you get your binders, your documents, Mr. Brdjanin, handed over to you in the afternoon?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, last night. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. And the interpreter, I suppose, she knows what her job is. You're the go-between, actually, the channel of communication between the accused and counsel for today. And you will treat that in strict confidence, because these are communications that are authorised to be strictly confidential. Thank you. So any preliminaries on your part, on your part? So let's bring the witness in, please. 7.50?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning to you, Mr. Tenic, and welcome to this Tribunal. Can you follow what I am saying in a language that you can understand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Is this your first time in this Tribunal, first time you're giving evidence before this Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The first time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So I will need to explain a few things to you. The first one being a very simple one, but it's the most important part for us. The lady who is standing next to you will be handing you a piece of paper on which there is the text of a solemn declaration that you are required to make here before you start giving evidence. It's the equivalent of an oath, an undertaking which you make with this Tribunal that in the course of your testimony you will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. So I invite you to take that document in your hands, read the statement aloud, and that will be your solemn undertaking.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. You may sit down. What's going to happen, Mr. Tenic, is that Madam Richterova, who is to your right and who is leading the Prosecution today, will put to you a series of questions. She will then be followed by Mr. Cunningham, the gentleman in the middle front row here, who is defending Mr. Brdjanin, who is the accused in this trial. I don't know if you've ever given evidence anywhere else before in your life, but the important thing that I need to explain to you is the following: That first you need to answer each and every question that is put to you, irrespective of whether it's being asked by the Prosecution or by the Defence, as fully and as truthfully as possible. No one expects you to know everything or to be a walking encyclopedia on the events that we're talking about, but what you know you must tell us, if you are asked the appropriate question. That's number one. Number two is: Please, if you really want to leave this Tribunal today and return to your home, please try to answer each question as briefly as possible. Don't answer more than you are asked. Just answer the question, the whole question, and nothing but the question. All right? Have you understood me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You have. So Madam Richterova will now take you over and start with her series of questions. Please. Examined by Ms. Richterova:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness. Would you be so kind and state your full name.

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: Good morning. I am Mehmed Tenic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Tenic, is it correct that you were born on 11 of September, 1957, in Teslic?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your ethnic origin is Bosniak and your religion is Islam?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You lived part of your life in the village of Barici, and later you moved to Teslic town; is it correct?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now I would like you to tell us something about the year 1991 and 1992, because we have already heard here the general information about the development in Teslic municipality. So I will ask you only a few questions relevant to this period of time. In your statement, you mentioned dismissals. Can you tell us: What do you know about dismissals, when they occurred, if they occurred?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: Well, what I know about dismissals, about people being fired from their jobs, well, something I know from my personal experience, and I also had this feeling, that is, I suddenly realised that people were disappearing all of a sudden from their jobs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that you know something from your personal experience. So can you be more specific? Did you know anybody who would be dismissed?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. I don't know the name of anyone, but I know it because -- you see, the man was missing from work and then you ask: Where is he? And mm [phoen], you know -- I mean, a man is simply not needed any longer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you also stated that people started disappearing from their jobs. What did you mean exactly by "disappearing"? Did they just stop working or just did they disappear from Teslic?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: No. They didn't disappear from Teslic, but they did not work any more. I worked for a company and I saw suddenly that those people who held executive posts were gone. Earlier on, there were Muslims and Croats there, but then gradually their numbers started decreasing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you are stating there were Muslims and Croats there, but then gradually their numbers started decreasing, are you referring to Muslims in executive posts or just generally Muslims and Croats in that company?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: People who held executive posts, more important posts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now I would like to move to the TO. You were a member of the Territorial Defence; is it correct?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Until when you were a member of the TO?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: I was its member until about the end -- no. Until about mid-1991.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what happened in mid-1991?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: I had to return the uniform, my military uniform, to the secretariat for -- no. Well, the Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was it only you or were there some other people who had to do the same?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: I don't know much about it. I couldn't say that I know a number of people, because I had to return it, and later on I heard that some other people had to do the same.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can we be again more specific? These people who had to return the uniforms, were they Muslim, Croats, or Serbs, or all three nations?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: Concretely, Muslims and Croats.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know whether the members of TO had to also hand over the weapons?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: As a member of the Territorial Defence, I would be issued with a weapon in case I was called for an exercise or something like that, because that was it. After you've done your military service, everybody who completed the service with the Yugoslav People's Army, after - I don't know - after returning from the army, he would be issued with this gear or become - I don't know - a member of the Territorial Defence. And then once or twice per year, as need be, one goes out for exercises or something. I wouldn't be able to tell you more.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So in fact, you, as a member of Territorial Defence, you didn't have weapon; you got it only when participated at some trainings. Is it correct?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know whether police reservists were in possession of weapons?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: Members of the reserve police had their weapons, of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And to your knowledge, at the time when you had to hand over your uniforms, was it the case that reserve policemen had to hand over their uniforms and their weapons?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: I wouldn't know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now I want to ask you about Crisis Staff. To your knowledge, was there any such an institution like Crisis Staff in Teslic?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: From what I know, all I know about the Crisis Staff in Teslic is what I heard from my father-in-law, who was friends with Mirko Devic. They were kums, bestmen at each other's weddings. They both liked to have a glass or two.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did they -- what did you learn from your father-in-law about the Crisis Staff? Just answer me this question.

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: He told me that kum Mirko had caused him great pain today. And I said: What happened? And he said: Well, kum told me that I couldn't go to the pub with him because they were having a meeting of the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who were the members of Crisis Staff, or what was the purpose of Crisis Staff? Did you learn anything about this from your father-in-law?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: I wouldn't know that. I know nothing about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Tenic, do you remember that sometime in 1992 there would be a special police or military unit which would arrive to Teslic from some other area?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: I remember it. Towards the end of May, a unit arrived from the direction of Teslic. Men or boys. I didn't know who they were or what they were. Later on I learnt that they were Red Berets.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Tenic, you said they arrived from the direction of Teslic. Did you mean to say from direction of Teslic? Because I asked you whether they arrived to Teslic, into Teslic.

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: I'm saying that that unit came from the direction of Doboj.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, Mr. Tenic. It was just -- I have to follow the transcript, what you are stating, and the translation was "from direction of Teslic." You said that they were Red Berets. Did you know who was the commander?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: Not at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you learn at some later stage who was their commander?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: Later on I did learn that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was the name?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: I know his nickname. I know people called him Piko.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And after this Red Berets arrived, what did you see? Were you in the town at the time when the Red Berets arrived?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: I was in the town then. They beat everybody, didn't ask who it was, what -- who the person was, what the person was. They simply beat all around.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So they were beating Muslims, Croats, and Serbs?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before I will go on, I want to ask you something about arming. Do you know whether, during the year of 1991 or first half of 1992, whether Serbs, Croats, or Muslims were arming themselves?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see people carrying weapons openly in Teslic or in the surrounding villages?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: In Teslic, I saw the reserve policemen carrying arms openly, and I did not see anything in the villages.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like to show you one document. It is Exhibit P1925.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: If we could place the English version on the ELMO and B/C/S version you can give to the witness. And if we could place the second page, please, on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Tenic, if you could have a look at the paragraph 1.8. In English version it is second page on the top. And it says: "All paramilitary formations and individuals illegally possessing arms and ammunition are called up and to hand them over to the municipal TO staff or the nearest military unit immediately or by no later than 15 hours on 11 May, 1992. After the expiry of this deadline, responsible organs will search and confiscate arms and ammunition, applying the most rigorous sanctions." And this document was issued by Teslic municipality Crisis Staff on 6 May 1992. The signature is Nikola Perisic. Mr. Tenic, do you know whether there was some announcement to hand over weapons in the Teslic municipality?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: There was an order for those who had weapons to return them. That was in Teslic. I didn't see that announcement. I only heard about this from some people from my village, you know. There was this disarming.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you heard from someone in your village, and is it correct that you are referring to the village of Barici?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you heard from people in the village of Barici that there was such an announcement?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And to your knowledge, did people hand over their weapons?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: That is something I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any weapons in Barici or in some other places?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: I don't know that either.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you at least hear that people from some villages would refuse to hand over the weapons?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I heard that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And from which villages?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: Rankovici village and Slatina, or Komusina village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know what happened after they refused to hand over their weapons?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Tenic, when we read this paragraph, there was that "after the expiry of this deadline, responsible organs will search and confiscate the arms." To your knowledge, were there any searches, either in Barici or in some other villages?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: I saw that in Barici. I experienced that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what can you tell us about these searches?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: In Barici, in my village, on that day when they arrived to carry out searches --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Tenic, I will -- I will stop you for a second. I know that it happened many years ago. Would you approximately remember the date? And when you are saying "they arrived," who you are referring to.

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: I am referring to the army and the Red Berets.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you are referring to army. Are you referring to the Serb army or JNA?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: I wouldn't know exactly, but the reserve troops of the Serbian army did not have tanks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So were they regular soldiers?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: I'm not sure, but I believe so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you, at the time when they entered your village, did you recognise any one of them?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: I recognised some people from the reserve policemen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you tell us the names of these people who you recognised?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: Tomo Mihajlovic, and there was another man whose nickname I know. I know that he was a regular policeman in Blatnica, and they called him Sujko.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And apart from Tomo Mihajlovic, did you name somebody else whose name you know?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: Nobody else.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And now can you tell us approximately when this happened, the date?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: On the 3rd or on the 4th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And 3rd or the 4th of which month?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: May -- I apologise. The 3rd or the 4th of June.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. So you stated that the soldiers, and also you now stated that there were reserve policemen, they entered your village on 4th of June. What happened after they entered the village?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: Everybody had to stand in front of their house. They had to have some piece of identification on them, either an ID or a passport. They would then enter the houses. What they were looking for, I don't know. They ransacked all the houses and they did it house after house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And after they finished searching houses, what happened then?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what happened to you that day?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: I had an ID with my address on it, my place of residence in Teslic. It was Proleterskih Brigada Number 7. And the guy told me: What are you doing here? I told him that I was here visiting my father, that there was nothing to eat down there, that I didn't have any food. Then he told me that I should have been in Teslic rather than here. He kicked me very strongly, and then, after that, I don't remember anything. Then I got up and I heard another order, and the order was for me to run towards the cemetery.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you were ordered to run towards the cemetery. Were there more men or was it only you who was running?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: All the men were asked to run.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you said that after you were hit, you do not remember anything. Do you remember -- you mentioned it at the beginning - that there was a tank in the village. Do you remember anything in connection with this tank?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: They hit me in front of my father's house. At that moment, I fell down, which was to be expected. Not that I fainted, but I simply wasn't aware of anything around me. And as I was running towards the cemetery, at some 200 or 300 metres away from my father's house, there was a tank. At that moment, I also saw some five or six lads who were on the ground in front of the tank, and I was also ordered to do the same, to lay down in front of the tank. And then the game started. Somebody would say: Tank, move forward. Run over them. And then the next order would be: No, don't move forward. And then we were also beaten up there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how long did it last?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: Twenty minutes or so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And after this, as you called, game, what happened then?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: Then we had to get up and start running again, this time with our eyes closed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where were you running?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: Towards the cemetery, the new cemetery.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you enter the cemetery?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: No, we didn't. We stopped short of the cemetery, in front of its entrance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Mr. Tenic, would you be able to recollect approximately how many people were there together with you?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: When I arrived there, there were already some 300 or 400 people there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they all men, or were they also some women?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: All men.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And would you be able to tell us which age range these men were?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: They were between the ages of 40 and 50, on average.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So they were -- were they people younger than 40?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember who was the youngest?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: At that moment, I didn't notice anybody in particular.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there anyone from your family there with you? I'm referring to immediate family.

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: My brother.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what happened in front of this cemetery?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: We had to stand there with our hands on our heads. I remember a van, a white van, arriving, and somebody asked for Vaso to step from the line. And then my cousin told me: Don't leave the line. You're not Vaso. You are Mehmed Tenic. This vehicle, this Golf, we call, I think it was, returned to the village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Tenic, I will stop you again for a second. When this person called out Vaso, is Vaso your nickname?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: Yes. All this time my nickname was Vaso.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You then stated this vehicle, Golf, returned to the village. What happened when this vehicle returned to the village?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: We remained standing there. The car returned. And on this second occasion, a guy who knew me was in the car. He told me to stop playing stupid and to step out of the line.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who was the person who knew you?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: Bobic, a former regular policeman.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We have Bobic. I think I heard some other name. Could you repeat his name, please, once again.

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: Not Bobic. Bubic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know his first name?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what happened after that?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: I entered the car. In the car, there was my friend, Sead Iriskic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where were you taken?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: I was taken to the SUP building in Teslic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you arrived in front of the SUP Teslic, what did you see?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: When I arrived in front of the SUP building in Teslic, I saw two or three persons lying down, covered in blood. I saw some reserve policemen. I saw people being beaten up, clubbed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you recognise anyone who was beaten?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: I recognised the former commander of the police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you, by any chance, remember his name?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: His first name is Sabinko, and I don't know his last name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember names, or did you recognise anybody who participated in the beating?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: I didn't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The people, did you recognise the policemen or soldiers who were in front of the SUP and who did the beating?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: At that time, I did not know their real names, but I found out later on who they were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us what did you find out later about their names?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: I learned that the main person among them was Piko and that he was a member of the Red Berets.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you learn some other names later?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And my last question to this is: Were they -- the people who did the beating, were they policemen or were they soldiers?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: Policemen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before I move further, I would like to show you Exhibit P1929.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Can you please place the first page on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm referring to the first paragraph in the middle, and it says: "About 50 Muslims and Croats have been arrested in Teslic. There is information --" first page for you, in the middle. "There is information that they were responsible for the organisation and creation of enemy military formations and the organisers of weapons, procurement, and distribution." This document is dated 5th of June, 1992, and it was prepared by Milos. You stated you were arrested on 4th of June. Does this document refer to your arrest?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were you responsible for organisation of military formations?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: I was not a member of any party. I was not a member of any organisation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you possess any weapon?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if I read for you the third paragraph, can you tell me whether you know anything about this: "There is still heavy presence of Ustasha formation in the area of the villages of Slatina and Komusina." You already mentioned that these two villages didn't hand over their weapons. Were you aware that there were some fightings?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: At that time, I was not aware of that. When I was in the camp, I heard about some fighting that had taken place. And while I was in the camp, I also heard some detonations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I will show you last document before we will move to your detention, and it is Exhibit P1250. And it is also in Teslic binder, and the date is 8th of June, 1992. The binders are organised in chronological order. And it follows directly the Exhibit P1929. I have extra copy for the ELMO. Mr. Tenic, I would like you to have a look at the fourth sentence -- no, I cannot -- I'm sorry. I cannot count. It's really the third sentence. And it says: "Our forces have engaged in successful mopping-up operation in the areas of Prijedor and Teslic." Did you hear anything about mopping-up operations?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear anything about shelling of witnesses -- of villages in Teslic, in the Teslic municipality?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: I only saw Stenjak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when was it?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: Stenjak was before I was taken away, a day or two days before that. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you see it yourself or did you receive this information from somebody else?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: I was watching Stenjak with my own two eyes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you see?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: Well, I saw people fleeing across fields. I saw houses being set on fire manually.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know -- and did you see that the village would be shelled?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: I saw, from the direction of Priletar [phoen] stadium that fire was opened. I don't know whether it was a tank or a gun or what. I know it was something. I mean, one of such pieces.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know who did the shelling?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: That, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: I'm done with these documents. And now I would like to focus on your detention.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I interrupted you when you stated that you saw several men lying in front of the SUP. You arrived to the SUP. What happened after your arrival?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: As I've told you, the first person I saw lying was Sabinko, former police chief, and that is when I was hit too. And they took us downstairs, to the cellar of the building. And as there was no room there, a policeman took us to another room.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say -- when you say "they took us," who was there with you?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: Well, I think that it was those Piko's Red Berets.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Was that what you meant? Because I don't think that's what you meant. Who was there with you? Who -- you were taken with others down to the basement, no?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Madam Richterova wants to know who the others were that were taken down with you to the basement, not who took you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Hasan Iriskic, Sead Iriskic, Huso Kopic, Nazif Kopic, and I can't remember who else was there with me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said you were taken to the basement. Were there already other people locked in the basement?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know approximately how many?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: No, I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you recognise anyone from these people?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you stay together with them or -- I'm sorry. You already answered: "There was no room there. A policeman took us to another room." In the other room, how many of you stayed in that other room?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: Seven or eight; I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did you stay in the basement of the SUP?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: I wasn't in the basement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I apologise. So how long did you stay in the building of the SUP?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: All night.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And after this night, did you stay in the SUP or were you transferred somewhere else?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: After that night, we were taken to the Territorial Defence building. That is what it was called at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While you were in the SUP, did you receive any food?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you receive any water?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: A litre and a half bottle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have any toilets?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you sleep?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: On the floor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have water to wash yourself?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And while you were in the SUP, how were you treated?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: Nobody touched us in SUP that night, because that policeman knew Iriskic, so he put us away and told us not to know anything, just to keep quiet.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say that nobody touched you that night. Are you referring to your group of approximately seven or eight people?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: I am.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether people who were in other areas of the SUP, how they were treated -- I'm sorry. How the people who were in other areas of the SUP were treated?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: I could only hear cries of pain, but I don't know anything else.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you interrogated when you were in the SUP building?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you told why you were taken in the SUP?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please come closer to the microphone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you come closer to the microphone? The interpreters cannot hear you. And you already mentioned that later you were transferred to the Teslic TO building.

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were all the people who were kept in the SUP transferred to the TO building, or, to your knowledge, were they transferred in some other place?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: I don't know whether everybody went, but people were coming out of the basement, and we came out. I don't know if all of them did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you arrived to the TO building, where were you taken in the TO building?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: Their former storage room, warehouse.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you arrived there, how many people were there together with you?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: Why, about 40, 50.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did this number vary during your stay?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: Yes, later on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know approximately what was later the number of people who were kept in the TO building?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: About 100, maybe 120.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they all men?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: Yes, they were all men.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any soldiers among them?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you receive any food while you were in the TO building?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: No, not that day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And later, did you receive any food? And if yes, how often?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: A sandwich once a day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you receive water during the whole time you were in the TO?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: We had a 10 litres of water, a cannister of 10 litres, and that was it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This 10 litres was for everybody who was in the warehouse?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: Everybody, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have toilets?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what did you do when you wanted to use toilet?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: Well, we urinated in the cannister.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: And could the witness please repeat.

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: And if we needed to defecate, we risked it and went outside, I mean risking the beatings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you need -- for a moment I thought I heard you say that you needed the witness it repeat something. I'm addressing the interpreter who is translating from B/C/S to English. Do you still require the witness to repeat any of his statements?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: No, thank you, Your Honour. The witness said the explanation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You stated you were risking the beating. Were you beaten if you wanted to use the toilet, or were you beaten on the way to toilet? Can you please explain this.

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: Well, you have to knock on the door if you want to do it. You have to put your hands on the head, and then you move towards the WC. Then you're hit once or twice; depends.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you sleep?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: On the concrete.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have any blankets?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you able to wash yourself?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you able to change your clothes?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you shave yourself?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When were you released from that TO building?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: I was released 30 or 40 days later; I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You don't know the date, exactly the date when you were released?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I can refresh your memory from the statement, on the page 5, you stated that you were released on 17 of July, 1992. Is it correct, or you do not remember it?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: I think that was the date, thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any diseases spread in the TO among the inmates?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: Well, there were lots of people suffering from diabetes, and there was a lot of dysentery.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether the people who suffered from diabetes or suffered from other diseases, whether they received any medical attention?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who were the guards in the TO?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: I know two of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us their names?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: Tomo Mihajlovic and Milorad Panic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they members of the Red Berets, these people, or you didn't know whom they belonged?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: Not then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to ask you one question in connection with these Red Berets. Did you hear the name Mice, Mice group?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: I've heard it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you hear about this Mice group?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: Well, I heard that those men, that Mice were part of a Green Berets [as interpreted], sort of Teslic guys.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you know or did you learn at some stage whether people who guarded you in the TO were member of this Mice group?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, because I am getting a little bit confused. Usually, until now, we have always associated the Green Berets with Muslim, Bosniak groups. Did the witness say that the Mice group, or did you intend saying that the Mice group was part of a Bosniak organisation? Because the Green Berets that we have heard of so far have always been Bosniak.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I think it was -- it --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please repeat which group this Mice group was part of? Was it Green Berets or Red Berets?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: Red, Red Berets.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I didn't notice in the transcript the word "green."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Then you can proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before this clarification, my question was: Did you know or did you learn at some later stage whether people who guarded you were in the TO, were members of the Mice group?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: It was afterwards that I learned that Tomo Mihajlovic and Milorad Panic were in the Mice group.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How were you treated during your stay in the TO?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: I was taken out for a beating a couple of times, never any questions, never any reasons given, only because I was called Vaso and was that nickname.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said you were beaten. Can you be more specific? Who did the beating, and did they use -- or the person who beat you, did they use any tools to beat you?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: As a rule, it would be those wooden batons or cords, all types of objects, boards.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who did the beating?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: Well, at that time you can't see who that is, because it is usually at night-time. You are not allowed to look. You have to face the wall. You have to have your hands on the wall, and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you recognise at least the uniform of this person who did the beating? Were they policemen, reserve policemen, or soldiers?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This beating, did it take place every day or just on several occasions?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: The worst beatings we received when men from Rankovici were brought. Nobody could stand then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they beat you all, or did they just select -- did they select only some people for beating?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: I said all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you witness that someone would die in the TO?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please tell us, what did you see?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: A young man was brought, whom I knew, who used to work with me for -- in a private business. I can't remember his last name, but I know his first name was Zlatan. He asked me to give him a pillow and to cover him with something, and he died around 4.00 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This Zlatan, can you describe, just briefly, in which condition he was when he was asking you for some help.

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: When I pulled up his T-shirt, well, he was -- he was all blue from the beating.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And he -- was he brought to the TO in this condition, or did he sustain these injuries in the TO?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: He was brought to the TO in that condition.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know where he was brought from?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you witness anybody else who would die in the TO?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: In the TO building, nobody else died except Zlatan.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your statement, if I can again refresh your memories, you mentioned that there were two young guys who died in the TO.

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: The other one died in the hospital in Teslic. He was taken there and died the same day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you see this young guy before he was taken to the hospital?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: I didn't pay attention to the young man, but I could see that he was tall and quite young.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see that this young guy was beaten in the TO?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: Since the authorisation had come that those who were injured or ill could stay lying down, and I had been hit in the back forcefully so that I couldn't stand. And as two came in, I saw how this young man was hit with the rifle butt in his back. And for a couple of days, he could only move his fingers. But then we asked them for a favour and they took him away, and afterwards I heard that he had died in the hospital.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You stated that the worst night was when they brought some men from Rankovici. Do you still remember this statement?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember who participated in the beating that particular night? Was it the same people who did the beating throughout your detention, or were these people -- or was it somebody else?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember name Boban Jovanovic?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was this person?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: That person had brought little Zlatan in, him and his friend, his best friend. I can't exactly remember the name of the other lad, but that other lad had told me that Boban and somebody else - I can't remember his name - had beaten him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This Boban Jovanovic, did he stay in the TO and did he participate in beatings, or did he leave after he brought Zlatan?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: He only brought him in and left.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During your stay, was there any occasion when large amount of people would be taken away and never seen again?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did this happen?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: I think after some three or four -- no, seven days after I was brought to the TO, they started calling out some people and taking them away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember any names of people who were taken away?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please state their names.

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: To begin with, I know Rasim Galijasevic, Mesud Kopic, a Croat -- no. His name escapes me, but I know him. Himzo Jasarevic. That's all I can remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you remembered it better when you gave the statement and you listed a few more names?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: Well, you know, it begins to fade slightly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know the names of people who took them away?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You can -- we are going to stop for a break now, but you can proceed with mentioning the names one by one and ask him whether he knows those persons, whether he remembers the name, and whether he could enlighten us. Thank you. Twenty-five minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I address the Court briefly? I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Cunningham.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Judge, if I might address the Court briefly. First of all, Mr. Ackerman was not feeling well, so he asked your permission to leave, and so he's not going to be with us the rest of the day. I'm ready to go forward. Secondly, during the break on a sheet of paper I wrote down the exhibits that I would be using -- anticipate to use in my cross-examination. I put them on a Post-it note in front of the usher so I wanted it give her some notice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Cunningham.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Ms. Richterova, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before the adjournment, I got permission to read you the names of people you mentioned in your statement from 17 of March, 2000, as people being taken away. It was Rasim Galijasevic; is it true? Himzo Jasarevic?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: I remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mesud Kopic?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: Yes, I remember him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Nihad Medic?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that. He was a professor, a teacher, that is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Victor Tibetanac?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: Tibetanac. I remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And one Lugonic?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: I remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. Sorry to interrupt you. I hate doing this, Madam Richterova, but we'll leave it now. When you referred to Nihad Medic, you said yes, I remember that. He was a professor. In your statement you also referred to a professor Midhad Midjic, who was all covered in wounds and who a meat axe or a hammer -- is it the same person or are we talking of two different persons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Midjic, Midjic is a professor. I know Professor Midjic personally. He sported a beard. And Nijad is also a professor or a teacher and he was also beaten up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So we're talking of two persons, one is Midjic and the other one is Medic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I know Midjic personally, and the other person I don't know so well. I know that his name is Nihad, but I'm not sure about his family name.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also mentioned in your statement two names, Petrovic and Panic. These two men, did they participate in taking away these people who I just listed?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: I don't know it for a fact, but I suppose so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were in the warehouse and these people were taken out, how did it happen? Were they called to go out or did someone come inside to take them away?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: Their names were called and then they had to go out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you see the person who called them?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I would like to ask you one more question just to clarify from your statement. You again mentioned Panic, and in that case, Milorad Panic, and Boban Jovanovic -- I'm sorry. My fault. You mentioned Boban Jovanovic in connection with the death of the other young boy who later died in hospital. Was this Boban Jovanovic involved in the beating or maltreatment of the other young boy who later died?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: I said that I suppose that Boban was there, because I know Boban from a very early age.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But did you see Boban Jovanovic beating this other guy who died later in hospital?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't see him beating him, but I saw him running past him and hitting him with a rifle butt in the head.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The people who are -- who you mentioned that you saw as being taken away, were there only these six men, or were there more people who would be taken away and never seen again?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: I know of only those that I mentioned. I don't know of any others.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what happened to these people you mentioned?

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Judge, I'm going to object to that. It's going to be hearsay unless he can establish who his source is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But we are having hearsay evidence all the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: And I understand that, Your Honour. I'm just --

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: I will rephrase my question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you learn from a particular person what happened to any of these people whom you mention in your statement?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: Not at that time, but later on I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did you learn later on?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: When I left the camp, I heard that they had been killed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From whom did you hear this information?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: From Mesud Kopic's father.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And to your knowledge, was anybody from these people ever found either alive or dead?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: I know that Kopic was. I don't know about others.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Kopic was what?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I heard later on about an exhumation during which his body was -- his remains were found and buried in his village. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know the place of the exhumation, the name of the place of the exhumation?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: I heard that, and I know that the name of this place is Bebe.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Your Honour, we already -- we didn't see exactly the exhumation in Bebe, but we saw the exhumation in Hanifici. And on the same tape is also the exhumation which took place in Bebe, and also we have the report, and both the report and the video were exhibited under P2018 and 2019 respectively.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Richterova.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like to show you, before we go any further, a few photographs. They have been exhibited under P1955.1 until 10. These are identical copies. If you could have a look and tell us whether you can see -- can you give them to the witness? And if you can see the TO building on any of these pictures.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Put them on the ELMO, please, rather than giving them to the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the Presiding Judge please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Sorry. Let's put them on the ELMO, please, rather than give them to the witness. The first one. And there we are seeing on the ELMO Exhibit Number P1955.1.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: What was my intention is if the witness first could go through these photographs and identify the picture on which is the TO building.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. We can do that one by one, and the usher will put them on the ELMO one after the other. Yes, but he hasn't answered the question as yet. What do you see on this first photo, the one which was the ERN number 0219-4087? What are we seeing there? Do you recognise that building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I can't tell you. I don't recognise the building.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Next photo. We are looking now at Exhibit number P1955.2, with ERN number 0219-4088. Look at that photo, sir. Do you recognise that mosque, or that building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Next photo, and we are now looking at Exhibit P1955.3, with ERN number 0219-4089. Looking at that building, sir, do you recognise it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Next photo. And we now have on the ELMO Exhibit number P1955.4, with ERN number 0219-4091, showing a building, or one building. Do you recognise that building, sir, the main building that you see on that photo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. And what are we looking at on that photo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On the other side, there used to be an entrance, and this building used to house the Teslic radio station. And in the basement of this building, there were people.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the left-hand side corner, we can see the remains of one building. If we can quickly could have a look at P1955.5, which is the next picture. Is it the part -- we can now see a building whose one part we were able to see on the previous one. Can you recognise this building?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: This is the Teslic SUP building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you said, during your testimony, that you saw some people lying on the ground and people being beaten, where did you see it? Can you point at the place where these people were lying? You have to point at the picture in the -- on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: Sabinko was here, where the car is. Piko came from here. This is where he was standing. The reserve policemen were standing here, as well as the regular policemen. Piko came from here, to this place, and asked: Where are you bringing these guys from? And somebody said: From Barici. Then he hit Sabinko first and then he hit me and then he shouted to the reserve policemen and ordered them to start beating the former commander of the police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we show the previous picture with the radio station? Did you see anyone close to that building maybe being beaten or lying on the ground? The P1955.4, if the usher could --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you want -- better place --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's put the previous photo on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Here. Three men were lying here, in front of the staircase.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we place now Exhibit P1955.6.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. For the record, we are looking at Exhibit P1955.6, with ERN number 0219-4096. Do you recognise that building, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. So tell us what we are looking at.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I recognise this building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is it? What is the name of this building?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: This used to be the TO building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you show us in which area you were locked, if it is possible from the outside.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: First of all, let's say: This is the front of the building or the back of the building or the side of the building? Can you tell us what we are looking at?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the front of the building that faces the street.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And were you kept in in the front of the building or in the back of the building or any other place in this building that you could tell us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We were exactly here, in this part of the building.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So in the front?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This used to be a storage, and it is in the front part of the building.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: I'm done with the photographs for now, but I would like to show the witness a sketch which was prepared by the witness during his interview in 2001, and it was attached to his statement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You prepared it as a sketch of the TO warehouse. Can you please just briefly describe what we can see? And first, what is the side facing the street, the front side of the building?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: This here is the front of the building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where were you located?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: I was exactly here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have your own designated places, or you can stay wherever you wanted?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: You couldn't stay just anywhere.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what was the normal routine when someone entered to the room? What did you have to do?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: I'm afraid I didn't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were kept in the warehouse. Did you stay the whole time in your place or were you able to walk around within the warehouse?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: I could move about, but when they entered the premises, I had to be in my own place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you kept only in this warehouse or were you allowed to go out, any time during your stay, from 4th June to 17th of July?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: When there was no water, then two guys were allowed to go out and bring water when we ran out of water.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But I'm asking whether you all were, at any time, allowed to go out of this warehouse, for a walk, to do some work, or did you stay the whole time inside of that building?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: No. We were inside all the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when the people who were called in June, and you never see them again, can you tell us where you were at that time and where were the people or the person who called these men on -- can you show us on this sketch where was your location and where was the person who called them out?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: I was here, as I've already told you. Rasim was here, that is, Rasim Galijasevic. Himzo was here. And little Kopic was here. I believe that Midjic, Professor Midjic was here, but I can't be sure about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the guard who called them, where was the guard?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: The guard would call our names from this room here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And he did it on that occasion as well?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: Yes, from this room.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you didn't see who he was?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: I'm done with this piece of paper.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Tenic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Are you tendering this sketch an exhibit in evidence or not?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: I am not tendering this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: According to your statement, you were released on 17 of July, 1992. I would like to show the witness an exhibit, P1930. This document is dated 6th of July, 1992, issued by Teslic Municipal Assembly, signed by Nikola Perisic. And I would like to place the last page, the page number 4 in English, on the ELMO. And if the witness could go to the last page of his version. And I am referring to paragraph 16 and 17. The paragraph 16 says: "Prepare a list of apartments and family houses that have been abandoned by their occupiers or owners for whatever reason or who were not in their house or apartment during the inspection by the civilian protection unit." Can you see this paragraph? Mr. Tenic, can you see the paragraph, what I just read? It was paragraph 16 on the last page.

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And paragraph 17 says: "Start moving people into the houses and apartments referred to in the previous item, giving priority to the families of those killed or wounded and to refugees." When you were released on 17 of July, did you go back to your apartment?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: I came as far as in front of my apartment, and I knocked on the door. And the door was opened by a woman wearing black. She asked me what I wanted, and I asked her if I could collect my belongings and explained that I had previously lived here. She told me to go away, and she said: I myself lost two members of my family on Stenjak, and if you don't go away, I'll call the police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you allowed to take your things from that apartment?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where did you go after you left the place where you used to live?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: I went to my father's in Barici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did you stay in Barici?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: I don't remember exactly, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Did you stay days, weeks, or months, or years?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not long. A month or maybe two months or so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you leave the municipality on convoy, in organised way, or did you leave it on your own?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: I did it illegally.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know whether other people were leaving as well?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: I heard that people were leaving in great numbers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you notice when this departure started, was it only after you were released in July or was it already before, let's say in May, June, before you were arrested?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: After I was released from the TO, I noticed that people were leaving.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were they also leaving before you were arrested?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: They were leaving. For example, I took my wife away before I was arrested. I was afraid because the situation became a bit unpleasant in Teslic. I don't know how else to put it. Blank pages inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Pages 16887 to 16899.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said you left illegally. Did you pay someone to take you away?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: I had to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Whom did you pay?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: A truck driver.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether there was some organised way how to leave the municipality?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: I only heard about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you hear?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: You signed that you're renouncing your property and then you can take a convoy to Novi Sad or Subotica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that you had to renounce your property. Do you know where such a person needed to go to renounce his or her property?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you sign over your property?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you also said that after a person would sign over the property, that they can take a convoy. Do you know who organised these convoys?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before you left -- and my one more question in this respect to your departure - was it in 1992 when you were asked -- when you decided to leave?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: I didn't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you leave the municipality in 1992 or later?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the time you were still in the municipality, did you witness or did you see any mosque or Catholic churches as being destroyed or damaged?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: I saw the church in the centre of the town, demolished, and in Barici, I saw the mosque.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in Barici, did you witness when the mosque was destroyed? Were you there in the time when the mosque was destroyed?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: Close to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you just very briefly describe what did you see?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: I saw then a few guys get off it, enter, and half an hour or an hour later, they left, and 120 -- and when the van had moved a hundred or 200 metres away, one could hear a powerful explosion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did it happen? During the day or during the night?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: Night.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when did it happen? Before you were arrested or after you were arrested? I'm sorry. Before you were arrested or after you were released?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: After I was released.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it was before you left the municipality?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The church in Teslic town, when was it you saw it damaged?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: I don't remember the exact date.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It will be enough for me if you could state whether it was, again, before you were arrested or after you were released.

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: After the release.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in which way the church was damaged?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: Well, there was only one side of it, and that was pulled down too. One side, where there was a picture of something.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see any other mosque being damaged or destroyed, apart from the one in Barici?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: I saw one in Ruzevic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Can I show the witness four photographs? It is P1955.7 until .10.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if you could recognise on any of these pictures the mosque which you would know.

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So, for the record, we are looking at Exhibit P1955.7, with ERN number 0219-409 -- I can't see the last digit. 99. Yes. And your answer to Madam Richterova's question is you don't recognise this building, no?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Next photo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The following, P1955.8, the ERN is 0219-4100.
