utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The following picture is P1955.9. The ERN is 0219-4101.

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the last one is P1955.10.

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: I know this one. This is Ruzevici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The ERN is 0219-4103. When did you see this mosque? Was it before you were arrested or after you were released?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: After the release.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what happened to this mosque, who destroyed?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: I'm done with the pictures. I have only a few more documents for this witness. If we can show the witness Exhibit P1931.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This document was issued by public security station Teslic on 8th of July, 1992, and it says, in its first paragraph: "About 40 Muslims and Croats have been massacred in the Teslic municipality by a group of criminals from Doboj. In addition, in only 20 days, the same group caused material damage of several million German marks to the Teslic municipality. They raped a large number of girls and women of all nationalities, which has caused fear among the citizens." This document was signed by Predrag Radulovic. First, did you know Predrag Radulovic or did you see this person in TO camp?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: Once.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what was his nickname?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: Pile.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the occasion when Predrag Radulovic came to the TO?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: Pile came after those guys were taken away and told us he didn't know what was happening and who was doing that, and that it would not happen again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After he left, were you immediately released or did you stay in the camp for some other time, for a longer time?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: No. We were released after that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how soon after his visit you were released?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it the following day or was there some period?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: No. A little bit longer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And about 40 Muslims and Croats were massacred. Did you learn later, or at the time of your detention, that these people were massacred or were killed?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: I heard about it later.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear that a group of people from Doboj did it?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what did you hear? Who did it?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: I don't know much about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: I would like to show an exhibit, P1932.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This document was issued by Teslic Lower Court on 11 of July, 1992, and it was signed by Nenad Kovacevic. It's the list of people that an investigation shall be conducted against the following accused persons. Can you please have a look on the first page and the second page. There is a list of names. And can you tell us whether you know anyone from this list of names?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: The first one I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know the first one or you don't know the first one?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: No. Sorry, not the first one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The first one is Pijunovic Miroslav, nickname Piko. Do you know this name or the person, or not?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: The name is familiar, but -- the person, no, I don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned that person with the nickname Piko was the one who was present in front of the SUP. Is it the same person as mentioned in this report or not?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: Miroslav Pijunovic Piko is the same person.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you go quickly, because I gave you an opportunity --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Tell him -- witness, go through the list. We don't need to ask you with each and every -- with reference to each and every particular name that there is. Go through it, take your time, and from that list, see if you know anyone, and tell us -- if you could give us any information on any of these persons.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I know Stojan Djuric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you see this person either in the SUP or in the TO building?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: Stojan, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know anybody else from this list?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now I want to -- I want you to go to the page 3 of your version, and it is also page 3 of the English version. And there is the explanation of -- because -- the reasoning of the investigation. And you had the opportunity to read these reasonings. Does it reflect accurately what happened, to your knowledge? Does it reflect accurately what happened in Teslic and in the TO building?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: First of all, has he seen this document before?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Yes. He saw this document during his proofing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. So you don't -- we don't need to give him much time to read it through completely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct that people were arrested?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: I didn't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday you had opportunity to read this document, and I would like to know whether the content of this reasoning reflects accurately what happened to you or what happened in Teslic. My first question is: Is it correct that people were arrested?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Illegally confined?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you ever told the reason why you were detained in the TO?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct that people were killed?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What can you tell us to the statement that they falsely introduced themselves to the civilian and military authorities as national security employees of the Doboj security service centre? It is the second sentence of this reasoning.

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: Incorrect.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you elaborate on this, in your opinion, why this statement is incorrect?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: Because they were civilians.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who were the civilians?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: Rama Skopljak [phoen] was with me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm referring to these people who are --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think we have a hell of a confusion here. Let's separate them straight away, because he definitely misunderstood you completely. There was no reason why he should have misunderstood you, but he has misunderstood you, because you were obviously referring to the man who supposedly came from Doboj, not to your village mates or other Bosniaks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So my question was: If you can make a comment whether the fact that Miroslav Pijunovic, aka Piko, and others, whether they falsely introduced themselves to civilian and military authorities?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: How do you suppose that the witness can answer that question?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: I withdraw this question. I withdraw this question, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We also mentioned that you heard about this group of Mice.

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: We have, Your Honours, the file on Mice group, which I would like to distribute it to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And this document which I was just reading is part of this file. And this Mice file contains the statements of all the people who were arrested and accused.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Has it been disclosed to the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: It was disclosed to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: When?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: It was disclosed many months ago.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And I will let you know in a second when exactly. I would like to give these ... This document was disclosed to the Defence on 29 of October, 2001.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, but when was the Defence informed that you were going to make use of this document?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: I informed him yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Cunningham.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: And that's correct, Your Honour, but I do not have a copy of that document with me, so I'd ask Ms. Richterova if there's by any chance an additional copy. And I realise it's somewhat voluminous.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Unfortunately, I do not have an additional copy of this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Chuqing. You can give Mr. Cunningham mine for the time being.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I am going to refer only to one statement, and I can give Mr. Cunningham this one particular statement which I am referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: And I appreciate that, Your Honour, but during the break, at our next break, I'd still like the opportunity to at least look through that and I appreciate the Court's indulgence --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, you are 100 percent right, because I don't relish the idea at all that -- I know now that I have, I don't know how many pages, right in front of me, and you're going to refer only to one particular part from that bundle. And I don't know what the rest is all about. So --

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I apologise that we hand over this file at such a late stage, and we are calling a witness who will talk about all the criminal files and will give a detailed explanation about the criminal procedure --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Anyway, let's go -- let's proceed, hoping that we won't encounter --

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: I would like to show the witness only one page from this file, which is in English version L0059796 until 59801. And in B/C/S version, if the witness can be shown the second page, in the middle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the paragraph starts: "Sto se tice oduzimanja imovine." In English, it is -- in English, it is: "As far as I know --" "as far as I know, these people voluntarily donated the money for the Serbian military and were released after that." The whole paragraph refers to Croat and Muslim citizens who gave money to the Serbs during the interrogation. Would you agree, to your knowledge, that Muslim and Croat citizens who were interrogated in the TO or the SUP building, that they would give, voluntarily, the money and donate this money for the Serbian military?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: I disagree.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it -- did anything like that happen, or did --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Usher, could you put the document on the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you agree with this statement or the situation was different than stated in this statement?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: The real life was different.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what do you mean? Can you elaborate on this?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: All the money, watches, rings, all the valuable jewellery had to be handed over. And as far as I know, nobody got it back.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you stated that this Piko was in the SUP, and this Piko was, among others, charged as one of the Mice group. And I would like to exhibit this file who contains the statements taken in Teslic in July 1992, statements taken from all the members of the Mice group, and I would like to tender this file into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Exhibit number?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: The exhibit number would be P1969.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Tenic, did you hear, any time during your detention or after you were released, that the members of Mice group were arrested?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: I heard about it later.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you also hear that the members of Mice group were released shortly after the arrest?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: I heard that too later.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: This is the last document which I want to show the witness. It's Exhibit P1935, and it is a newspaper article from 23rd of July, 1992. The publication is Glas, and the headline is: "The Notorious Mice Are Free." And I intend to read only the first sentence, which says: "As we have learned unofficially, the notorious Mice from Teslic are free again. In spite of dozens of the most serious criminal offences which they committed against the inhabitants of Teslic in June of this year, they were released by the High Court in Doboj for reasons which are still unknown."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To your knowledge, were -- after they were released, were they ever convicted of any crimes which they committed in Teslic?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever see anybody who was in Teslic, who was in TO building, and who was member of the Mice group or Red Berets? Did you see such a person at some later stage, again in Teslic or in Doboj?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: I did see one, but I can't remember what his real name was. And since I was in house detention after I was released, I wasn't allowed to move about, move away from the house in Barici. And that man came to the TO too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if we are talking about, let's say, the years 2000, 2001, 2002, have you ever seen, walking, anybody of these people in Teslic, Doboj, or in some other areas in Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I've concluded my examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Richterova. Mr. Cunningham.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: May I proceed, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, but before we do so, can we have an indication as to whether we require the presence of the next witness here this morning, or not? Because if we don't, I wouldn't like to see anyone here waiting in a room by himself for an hour, or for any time, for that matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: My guess is my cross-examination -- I'm going to surprise the accused and not say 45 minutes, but I think my cross-examination is an hour, maybe a little bit more. So --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So we have half an hour now. Then we start at 12 -- at 1.00. You decide, Madam Richterova. My rough guess is that if Mr. Cunningham has an hour or a little bit more, I wonder if we need to bring him over. I don't know. It's up to you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: I asked to bring the other witness at 12.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, but it's --

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: I understand -- I understand your point. We are scheduled other witness for tomorrow. Luckily I'm not using any exhibit with that witness, so --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, but I have gone through his statement, and it's not a short statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: It is not a short statement, but I believe that it will be faster than this testimony. But I would -- of course, I would like at least to start with that witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So I would suggest that you bring him over at about 1.15, and hopefully see if we can give him half an hour. But I don't anticipate more than that. And please do make it clear to him, whoever is going to be in contact with him, that not to be surprised at all if nothing happens today.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Will do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right? Thanks. Mr. Cunningham.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Cross-examined by Mr. Cunningham:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Tenic, good afternoon. How are you today?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon. I'm very well, thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good. I'm glad to hear that. I'm going to ask you some questions, and much as you did with the Prosecutor, please answer only the question I ask you, to the best of your ability. If you don't know, just let me know. Fair enough? I'm going to talk to you about some events that happened in your municipality. They may not be in order chronologically, and I'm not doing that to confuse you. That's just the way that I have it organised. So bear with me. One of the very first things that you talked about was the fact that a number of Croats and Muslims, Bosniaks, were dismissed from their jobs. I want to go back to the time in 1991, to go back to the spring of 1991/the beginning of summer 1991, say June 1991. How was the economy in your municipality? How would you describe it? Were a lot of people at work? It was as good as it was, say, in the late 1980s? How would you describe it?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: I can't answer that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Fair enough. In -- when the war with Croatia started, did that war have any impact on the local economy? By that I mean, did people start to lose their jobs because of the war?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were a locksmith; am I correct?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have your own shop or did you work with other people?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: I worked with others.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how many people did you work with in your locksmith shop? How many other employees?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: I first worked in Zanatstvo and later on I was employed by a private employer, and I worked with some five or six people altogether.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. When the war with Croatia, in Croatia, started, did any of the five or six people that you worked with, did any of them either get called up or leave work for another reason? And when I say "called up," I mean mobilised, called up into the military.

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the time that -- during your testimony earlier in the day, you talked about how you had been a member of the TO and that there came a time when you were required to turn in your uniform. Do you remember that testimony?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At any time before you turned your uniform back in, had you been called up, had you been mobilised into the military? And let me rephrase that, because I realise it's a poor question. You told us that you had to turn in your uniform to the TO barracks or office. Before turning it in, had you received an order to mobilise?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had anyone in your municipality received an order to mobilise, as far as you know?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You talked about - and I believe that was in your statement - how, in the winter and spring of 1992, February/March of 1992, you talked about in your statement that it was Serb reservists who were the ones that had weapons. Do you remember making any statement like that in your written statement you gave to the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: I remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you obviously did your duty for the JNA and were part of the reserves. Let me ask you this: Based on your knowledge and experience, when a reserve is called up, are they incorporated into the army or are they just in a separate reserve unit that acts separately from the JNA?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: I can't answer that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it because you don't know or don't remember?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. That's fair enough too. Were there checkpoints in the summer - excuse me - in the winter of 1992, around the municipality of Teslic, did you notice any checkpoints?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when did you first start to notice those, if you can recall?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: No, I don't remember the date.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Did you ever have to try to pass through the checkpoints that were set up?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were you successful in doing that?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: Not through all of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. You say not through all of them. Roughly, if you can tell us, what percentage were you able to get through? Could you get through 50 per cent of them, three-quarters of them? What is your best recollection?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: There were very few of those that I could go through.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the reasons that were given as to why you couldn't leave were statements like: The citizens of your municipality who were of a certain age, say age 18 to 60, had to remain within the municipality. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the military-aged men had to stay in the community. And did you see that order that military-aged men having to remain in the community, was that enforced against the Serbs, the Bosniaks, and other ethnicities?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your statement, the written statement you gave to the OTP many months ago, back on March 17th, the year 2000, you said this: "I know that during the end of 1991, all Serbs, Croats, and Muslims armed themselves. They usually brought those weapons from soldiers who were coming from the Croatian front lines." Do you remember making a statement like that?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: I remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So what you're telling us, that your recollection is, during that period of 1991, all the ethnic groups were arming themselves. And I believe, to be fair to you, in the very next part of that statement - and let me read it in English so you'll have the complete statement in front of you - that you said the following: "All those weapons had registration numbers and it was easy for the Serbs to trace those weapons and take them from the Croats and Muslims. I know that in March and April, that there were no more weapons among the Muslims and Croats." My question to you is this -- and judging by your yes answer, you recall making that statement back in March of 2000. My question to you is this: What was the registration system that allowed -- well, let me back up. It appears that those guns were bought on the black market, because they were purchased from people coming back from the Croatian front line. Would that be a fair statement?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: Could you please repeat that?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sure. You talked about how, in your statement which you've confirmed today, that the weapons that were purchased were usually purchased from people coming back from the front line. Do you remember making that statement?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: I remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it would be fair to say if people are buying weapons from people returning from the front line, they would be buying those guns out on the black market, they would be buying them illegally?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So my question to you is this, and if you know, fine; and if you do not know, that's equally well: How would the registration numbers be traced if these weapons were purchased on the black market?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: My aunt's son was in Croatia. He was on the Croatian front line, and he told me that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So the information -- the only source of the information you have that these weapons could be traced, the registration number could be traced, comes solely from a relative of yours?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the next part of your statement, and I think I read it to you again, but to be totally fair, I want to read it to you yet again to make sure that I get it totally correct --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Perhaps we could give him a copy of his statement straight away if you're going to refer, and later on I will be referring to the statement. I think it would be better if he has a copy in front of him all the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Of course, Your Honour. And by way of introduction, Mr. Tenic, obviously I do not speak B/C/S. I'm referring to the English copy. I believe the paragraph that I'm talking about will be on the second page, and it begins, at least the English version begins with the following statement: "I know that during the end 1991," just to help get you oriented. If you could read that paragraph that I just gave you the introduction to. In English, it looks like it's about six lines long. Read it to yourself, because I'm going to ask you about the very last sentence. I can tell by the nod that you're done. The very last sentence says: "I know that in March or April there were no more weapons among the Muslims and Croats."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the area you grew up in, your municipality, is very, very common for people to have hunting rifles. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it was common for people, for many people, to have pistols. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the -- you've mentioned two towns, and I apologise if I mispronounce them. One was Rankovici, and the other one was Slatina. And again, I apologise for my pronunciation. Do you remember mentioning those two villages?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: Slatina and Komusina. I believe these are the names of those two villages.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Let's talk about those villages. Those are villages that have largely a Bosniak population. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: In Slatina and Komusina, I'm afraid I did not understand.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is the majority ethnic group in those two villages that you've mentioned, is it Bosniak or another ethnic group?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: They're mostly Croats.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Are there any -- what about the town -- the village of Rankovici?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: Muslims.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, because I'm going to -- I want you to get oriented. If we look at the very next paragraph of the statement that you were reading, it says the following: "I remember that people from villages had to hand over their weapons, and I heard that people from Rankovici and Komusina did not do it."

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: I didn't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. I just wanted you to read the next paragraph so that you could confirm what I just read to you in English, which says: "I remember that people from villages had to hand over their weapons, and I heard that people from Rankovici and Komusina did not do it." And that's what you wrote in your statement that's in front of you right now. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So we have at least one village within your municipality that you've characterised as a Bosniak village, that didn't turn over their weapons. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know of or know an individual by -- living in Rankovici by the last name of Beganovic [phoen]?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: Beganovic?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Again, I apologise for my pronunciation, but I believe that's how it's pronounced. Do you recognise that name, first of all?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: There are quite a few individuals with that name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me -- and again, I apologise in advance for my pronunciation. The name S-u-l-j-o, Suljo, does that name, first name, ring a -- do you recognise it?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do recognise it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you aware that it was known that he had been supplying arms in the city or the village of Rankovici?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were not present, obviously, between -- you heard about the fighting in the two villages you told us earlier, but were you aware that during that fighting, that there were policemen of Serb nationality that were killed when the villagers didn't turn over their guns? Did you hear that when you heard about the fighting in those villages?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: I heard of all these things once I was released from the camp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And another thing, and tell me this: After your release from the camp, did you know that there were two officers who were ambushed and killed also in Teslic, two police officers?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't, not in Teslic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I'm speaking of Teslic, not the town of Teslic, but the entire municipality.

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: Yes, I've heard of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it was suspected that they were killed by Bosniaks still possessing arms. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's fair enough. Do you know who the president of the SD [sic] was in Rankovici, who the head of the SD [sic] was in the village?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: I haven't a clue.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever hear once you were released or while you were in custody that weapons were found in his home when a search was conducted?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: I don't know. No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, Mr. Cunningham, because we need to clarify this, at least for the record. When you asked the witness whether he knew who the president of whichever party you mentioned, it seems that the -- in the transcript we just have the first two letters, SD.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Obviously it should be SDA, Your Honour. That was my question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. So -- but I want to make sure that it was translated or it was interpreted accordingly to the witness. Do you confirm that you understood the question as referring to the president of the SDA party?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was not a member of any party in Teslic municipality, so I wouldn't know anything about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Go ahead, Mr. Cunningham.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: There's a brief area that I want to try to cover in the next three or four minutes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us, sir, that while you stayed in Teslic, you had your wife leave town to go stay either with friends or relatives. While you -- before you were detained, were you aware of Bosniaks leaving Teslic and going to Tesanj? And I know I'm probably mispronouncing that as well. Were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I know from your statement and what you've told us today, that you didn't -- you don't watch TV, but were you aware of programming that was coming, originating from Bosniaks in that area, in Tesanj?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: No, I wasn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before you were -- after you were released, were you aware that a War Presidency had been set up by Bosniaks in that area?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: No. No, I wasn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's fair enough.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm about to go into a different area and we're right on the cusp of a break, if the Court pleases.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We'll have a 25-minute break starting from now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Cunningham.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. With the Court's permission and the usher's assistance, I'd like to show Exhibit P1925 to the witness, and specifically, I'll be going to the second page, paragraph 1.8.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This Exhibit, sir, is a document issued by the Crisis Staff of the Teslic municipality on 6 May 1992 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: He's seen it already.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Okay. Just for the record, I wanted to clarify that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if we look at the very first paragraph on the second page, that paragraph being 1.8, you would agree with me that that is a directive that paramilitaries and individuals illegally possessing guns should turn them over. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: I know nothing about this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I'm just asking you to confirm what's in the record. It appears to you - correct me if I'm wrong - that it's a directive for people who are in illegal possession of guns, including individuals and paramilitaries, that they're to turn those guns in; would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. I'll move on, because the document speaks for itself. In the middle of May, you were not incarcerated, and that's when the Red Berets first -- according to your statement, that's when you first became aware of them. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you first become aware of them, then?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: I saw the berets -- well, I gave you the dates. It could have been the 28th or the 30th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: 28th or the 30th of what month?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: June, I think.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. I want you to look, if you have your statement that you gave on March 17th, 2000, available. I'd like to take you to - and I apologise if the paragraphs are different in your B/C/S statement - but one, two, three, four paragraphs down, the very last sentence of the fourth paragraph in the English version says the following, and I want to see if you can recall this your statement says this: "Later on the Red Berets came, the chaos started. They arrived in the middle of May 1992."

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: That's not what it says in my text.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It appears to me, even with my very, very limited knowledge, that the very paragraph, the very last sentence of the fourth paragraph, says May 1992. But let's don't get stuck on dates.

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry. You said the fourth paragraph, not the last sentence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Do you see that portion of your statement where you say that they came around the middle of May 1992?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: I see it, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you first saw the Red Berets, obviously they were wearing red berets, but how else were they dressed? What sort of military uniforms, if any, were they wearing?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: They were in olive-green/grey uniforms. Some had neck scarfs. That is what I saw.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you were at some time found out that they were from Doboj. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: I said they had come from the direction of Doboj.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Fair enough. Who was their leader? Who did you understand was their leader?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: I didn't know who the leader was at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you later come to find out who their leader was?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did find that out later on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who was the leader?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: Piko.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Once they arrived, they started beating on people on the streets irregardless of their ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And they operated in the town and were attacking people of all ethnic groups. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: Yes. They beat people all over the town. They didn't care who was what.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you aware that they even went to the Crisis Staff meeting and assaulted the members of the Crisis Staff of the municipality?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: I didn't know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. You were -- and when Ms. Richterova was asking you a question, she showed you - and I'm done with that document, Madam Usher - she showed you Exhibit P1969, which was a criminal record associated with the individual you call Piko. Do you remember seeing that document?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: With the Court's permission and the usher's assistance, can we show him again P1969, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Earlier we --

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: And I'm sorry to interrupt. It's only that I tendered into exhibit the whole file, and I was only reading from one particular statement from this whole file. So when Mr. Cunningham is referring to Exhibit P1969, he is referring to the whole file.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. I think your -- rather than objection, I think your observation is right. Perhaps you could --

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: I can clear it up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We can clear it up. We can have the English version put on the ELMO. At least we can look at the ERN numbers. And the same we'll do after that with the B/C/S version, if there is a B/C/S version. I would suppose that there is.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: That's fine, Your Honour. And I apologise to Ms. Richterova. I should have said an excerpt from P1969. And the ERN number for the page, we were looking at page 4, the English version. This was something that was pointed out to you earlier, sir. The ERN number is L0059799.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And to refresh your recollection, what was shown to you was the second paragraph that begins with the phrase: "As for the confiscation of properties from detainees or other citizens." Now, having seen that document, again, do you remember talking about it before the break?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: I think the witness has English version. He needs B/C/S version. And in B/C/S version, we are talking about second page. And it's second page, third paragraph, in the middle.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I remember it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, Ms. Richterova asked you questions about what this individual put in his statement, talking about the money that he took, and I want to ask you some questions about the Mice in general. While you were either in custody or released from custody, you came into contact with the Mice. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: I didn't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While you were in custody, while you were detained and while you were -- after your release, you saw the Mice personally?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: I did, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also had conversations with people, either while you were in custody or after your release, about the Mice and what they had done?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: To begin with, Mice was a group of people. There wasn't only one Mice.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I understand that. I'm speaking of the group as a whole.

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: One of them -- after I was released, I was at home then at my father's, and the one who used to beat me in tow came to that house and beat me again, which means that he stayed on in Teslic. That is how I made my conclusion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. And what you've just told us is the Mice beat you, and you saw them beat other people while you were in custody.

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: That guy, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And you saw other members of the Mice while you were held in the TO. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: I'm telling you that I learned it all later on, that they were called Mice and everything else, and about the berets.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And what you learned later on is that these people known as the Mice, for example, had been stealing jewellery, cash, personal property, from people in the municipality. Right?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: I said that they had taken it from us, that I had to turn over the money that I had on me, my watch, the jewellery that I had, that I had to turn it over when I was detained.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it wasn't just you; it was other detainees. Right?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you know, either from it happening to you or happening to someone from the municipality, they also took cars and vehicles from people. Right?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: I've heard about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And you know from what you saw happen in the camp that they were involved in the brutal beatings of people that were detained with you. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you also know, from what you saw or what you heard after your release, that the Mice were involved in the execution of individuals from your municipality?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. The Prosecutor asked you some questions earlier about the Mice and what happened to them in the courts, and I want to ask you some questions that follow up on the questions that she asked you. And if you know, that's fine; and if you don't know, that's fine. Did you know that the authorities in Teslic municipality requested a forensic team to help them in the investigation of the Mice? Did you know that?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know that -- and I want to make sure I have the terminology right. Did you know that an investigating judge of the Teslic Lower Court had ordered them detained?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: I know nothing about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Let me just move on. You know from what Ms. Richterova suggested to you and showed you in exhibits today that, for some reason, they were not prosecuted for the wrongs that they have done; right? You know that?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: Could you repeat it, please?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sure. As far -- and I'm going to rephrase it, and I'm not doing it to confuse you, but let me see if I can make it a better question. You know that the Mice have never been prosecuted, have never been brought to court for the wrongs that they have done in your community. Right?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: I do not know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's fair. Let me move on to another subject. I'm going to talk to you about your detention, and I'm not -- and I know that this is a little bit out of order and I'd just ask you to bear with me. When you testified earlier, you were shown Exhibit P1929.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: And with the Court's permission and the usher's assistance, I'd like to show you the B/C/S copy of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I believe the Prosecutor questioned you about the very first paragraph on the page, in the English version, the ERN number is L0040195. I want you to look at the B/C/S version of that to make sure that we are on the same page, that we're talking about the same document, before I ask you a question about it. Let me know when you're done reading the first paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: I've finished reading.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There's a sentence in there that reads as follows: "About 50 Muslims and Croats have been arrested in Teslic. There is information that they were responsible for the organisation and creation of enemy military formations and the organisers of weapons procurement and distribution." That's what that paragraph says, and I believe Ms. Richterova asked you: Is that you? Were you among the 50 people that were arrested? Do you remember when she asked you that?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: I remember that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you know that that statement refers to you?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: Why, because it says 50 arrested individuals, and I was in the camp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But I thought -- I thought - and correct me if I'm wrong - that at times the camp it up to 200 people in it.

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: I'll do it slowly. In the beginning, at the SUP, from what I could see in the bus, we were 40 to 50 people in the bus and we were lying on the floor. And when we got to the TO, groups started arriving from Rankovici, from Gornji Teslic, from Komusina, Banja Vrucica, and I stated that we were about 100, 120.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And in Rankovici and Komusina, those were the towns that -- at least Komusina was. Let me back up so I can make my question shorter. You told us that one of the towns that people started arriving from was from Komusina. Komusina is one of the towns that was a Bosniak town that was offering resistance, armed resistance, against the authorities. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: Incorrect.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. I'll just move on, because I'll get to another area. While you were in custody, you told us that an individual- and just to get you oriented, this is, I believe, close to the end of your detention, before your release - an individual by the name of Radulovic arrives. His -- I believe his nickname was Pile, P-i-l-e.

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And he made a speech to the detainees. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: He did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And he said -- and he provided you with some items. I want to say he gave you some food, gave the detainees food and cigarettes. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And he told you that the maltreatment, the mistreatment, would stop. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it wasn't that day, but shortly after that speech, is when you were released. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: Yes, shortly after that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I forgot to go over something with you while you were in detention, and I apologise for that. I'm not trying to confuse you. But I want to talk to you about one of the deaths, beating deaths, that you witnessed while you were in detention, and that death involved a young man, aged 17, by the name of Zlatan.

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: I said that he was 17 or 18.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. I'm not arguing with you over the age. I just have a question. You told us that you knew him from work. Where did you work with him at?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: He worked for a private metal shop.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And I don't -- I know I will show my ignorance of your country, but would you have known him working when he was 15 or 16? How old was he when you first came into contact with him?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: I said he was 17 or maybe 18.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I have a couple more areas to go over with you, and I'll try to do them as quickly as I can. Ultimately, arrangements were made for you to leave your municipality. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: Could you repeat the question, please?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To leave your country, certain arrangements had to be made. For example, you had to find the truck driver and pay the truck driver. Your family had to find the truck driver and pay the truck driver to get you out of the country. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: To begin with, I had to leave. I had to flee. And I found -- and it wasn't my family which paid, but I collected the money. And I didn't even pay the full amount.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And believe me, I'm not criticising you for what you did, but in order to leave, you had to leave illegally, with a counterfeit passport. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: Well, when you are travelling illegally, you don't need a passport.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Wasn't there a correction in your statement that came up during proofing that, with the assistance of a policeman, you got some -- a policeman pointed you or directed you to a place where you could get false travel documents?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: In Subotica, which is in Serbia, not in Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. But just -- that happened. That is, you got those --

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- documents? Okay. I see you answered the question. There's one final question, and again I apologise, because I'm going to go back to something that you witnessed. I believe you told us that at one time, you saw the former commander --

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: I'm sorry to -- I apologise. I didn't react quickly. But I can't see anywhere in his statement that --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the Presiding Judge, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's in the -- Madam Richterova, it's in the other statement of 13th June 2002.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's the last paragraph, where he makes some alterations or changes or explanations with regard to page 6 of his original statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: I can see. I really apologise for this interruption.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: I promise this is the last area I'll ask you about.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your testimony earlier today you told us that at one time you saw the commander, Sabinko, being beaten. Do you remember testifying about that today?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And he was - correct me if I'm wrong, but wasn't he being beaten by the individuals that you associated with being the Mice?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: I've stated, and my statement was given after all this. These people who brought me in were Berets, or Mice.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And the people that were doing the beating on Mr. Sabinko, were they the Red Berets, the Mice?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: Pika's men.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know, happen to know, what ethnic group Mr. Sabinko belongs to?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: He was a Muslim.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's all the questions I have, sir. I wish you a safe journey home.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Is there re-examination, Madam Richterova?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: There is no re-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Judge Janu, do you have any questions? We have some questions for you. It will soon be over. If you're too tired, we can postpone them, but we can finish now. I think it will be better for everyone. Yes, Judge Janu. Questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JANU
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, when you were describing us the death of one of these young boys, that older one, Zlatan, you mentioned also that there were 16-year-old boy. You didn't name him in your statement. You only said that he was from Rankovici. You said his family name was Begovic. Yes. And you said he was also severely beaten by Boban Jovanovic, and you also said that you asked for some guards to help him, but they didn't. Do you remember the name of this guard or those guards who were asked to bring some medical aid to this boy, or you don't remember?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: I can't remember the exact names of those who were standing guard at that time. No, I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JANU
utterances.text: You can't remember. Okay. And my second and last question is: Are you back at your house, or did you restitute this house, or are you still living abroad?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I think we should redact the last sentence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So be it. Yes. The -- where he's living now should not be communicated to the public. So it will be redacted, for your own security. Judge Taya, do you have -- I have a few questions to ask you. In your statement, apart from Tomo Mihajlovic and Milorad Panic, you had also mentioned Milovan Djukic and a certain person, individual, with the name of Petrovic. Do you remember these two persons at the TO building, being guards over there?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: I remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Were they policemen, military, or part of the Mice group?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: They were policemen. One of them was a policeman, and the other, I learned at the time, was a member of the Mice group.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Which one?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's take Zlatan now. Who would you say, according to what you witnessed, would be responsible for his death, directly, physically responsible for his death?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: I can't remember the exact name of the lad with whom Zlatan had been brought in, and this lad told me that they had been beaten by Boban and the other person whose name was Damir and whose last name I can't remember at the moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. But earlier on, when you were telling us about Zlatan and how he asked you for a pillow and he needed to be covered before he died, you told us that he himself told you who had beaten him up. Did he mention a name to you?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: He mentioned the names, but he was in such a condition that he couldn't really talk. So this other lad later on told me everything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And the other young man who in your statement you referred to as Enes Begovic, from the village of Rankovici, who would you say is responsible for his death, directly and physically responsible for his death?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: I would say that it was Boban, but I am not sure. I've told you that I saw him running past him and hitting him in the head with his rifle butt.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Now, am I right that Boban Jovanovic was from Teslic?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Was he there as a policeman, as a military, or as a member of Mice, part of Mice?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: He was a member of the Mice or the Berets. I don't know which one of those.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You have seen the list of the Mice group that were originally put under investigations and arrested or detained. I put it to you that Boban Jovanovic's name is not there. Could you think of a reason why his name would not be there if he participated in the killing of these two persons, young men?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: I wouldn't be able to say anything about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you know if Boban Jovanovic is still alive today?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: I've heard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Is Teslic now part of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Is Doboj part of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: Yes, but not all of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Did Boban Jovanovic have any connection with Doboj, that you know of?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you know if Boban Jovanovic still resides in Teslic today?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: According to what I've heard, he's in Sweden.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: In your statement, you said that: I heard that Boban Jovanovic is now in Sweden and that he got asylum. Why would he ask for and obtain asylum in Sweden if he resided before that in a town or in a village or in a municipality that forms part of Republika Srpska? What is he running away from?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Why would he seek asylum in a foreign country?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I only heard that he sought an asylum.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you know the Glas newspaper?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You've never seen the Glas newspaper?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: Glas? No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You were shown document 1935 before. Perhaps we can have it shown to him again, 1935. It's the Serb -- that's the name of the -- you've never seen that newspaper in your life, never come across that newspaper or heard about it?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: I may have, but I really never paid too much attention to its name. I'm sorry. This is the first time that I actually see Glas.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And you wouldn't know whether it's -- where it's published?

utterances.speaker: MEHMED TENIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. That's all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. You see me smiling, and that's because we have finished with you, and you should be smiling too, because now you can leave this courtroom and go back to your country of residence. Before you do so, however, I want to put your mind at rest that you will be given all the attention and assistance you require by our staff to enable you to return to your country. And on behalf of the Tribunal and the two Judges, Judge Janu from the Czech Republic and Judge Taya from Japan, I should like to thank you for having come over to give testimony in this trial. My last words to you is have a safe journey back home. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's go into private session for a while.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
